full_card.band: 8h tier. Frontier finds the redundant hashing quickly; difficulty is correctness under mtime/inode edge cases across four commands and cold vs warm cache. Weaker models cache only in-process or break equivalence. Band capped at 3: no dated public evidence.

full_card.deliverable: Agent-side change so dvc status, diff, commit and repro skip rehashing unchanged files (stat-keyed state/cache DB) while stdout, exit code and .dvc/lock bytes stay identical.

spike_plan.kill_if: Base cannot be built or tested offline in about 60 minutes; outputs differ across runs; or no change reaches 1.5x status speedup on the generator; or the reference cannot pass the same-size same-mtime scenario without hashing.
spike_plan.pass_if: Base builds offline and tests are deterministic; outputs are byte-identical across 3 runs; the 7a795f7 change or a stat-keyed cache gives at least 1.5x median speedup on status with the reference passing every scenario.
steps: Clone treeverse/dvc and dvc-data in a throwaway network container; confirm 7a795f7 and its parent and pin the parent as the base commit.
Create an offline venv of the base with pinned dvc-data and dvc-objects; confirm `dvc --version` and `pytest` (or a subset) run and record per-test results.

Write a small generator: 20k files across 5 stages, then run status on a warm tree, a mutated subset, touched-mtime-only files, and same-size same-mtime edits; capture stdout, exit code and .dvc/lock bytes.
Run the same workload 3 times on base and check the outputs are byte-identical across runs (determinism).
Apply 7a795f7 (or its equivalent) on top of base and rerun timing; if it fails to apply, port the raw-dir-object change by hand.
Check whether a naive stat-keyed cache breaks the same-size same-mtime scenario and whether the fixed reference passes it; if the reference fails, drop that scenario.
Test gVisor-like behaviour: run the generator and status in a sandboxed container and confirm mtime_ns and inode are stable across runs.

v1.summary: The seed is real: treeverse/dvc#7390 is a closed regression report and its fix PR #7597 merged as 7a795f7 on May 12 2022, with Apache-2.0 licensing confirmed. It is not killed, but it is conditional: the reference is undefined (2022 fix plus unspecified later state-DB work), smoke_build is empty so there is no offline build evidence, and a stat-keyed cache may contradict the same-size same-mtime hidden scenario, so the spike must settle these before the card is accepted.

v2.note: The regression and fix are real (#7390, fixed by PR #7597 as commit 7a795f7), but the fix is one lever: save and reload raw dir objects to avoid rehashing. The reported effect is only about 0.65s vs 1.8s. The 'state-DB follow-on work' meant to scale up the reference was not found, the pre-fix hash is unpinned, and the dvc-data/dvc-objects licences are unverified. The same-size, same-mtime edit scenario conflicts with DVC's own stat-keyed state: a correct reference would report that file unchanged while the base reports it changed, so the gate is ill-defined. At 6h frontier for an 8h tier with a single fix, the task is short and one-lever.
